# Sound control (pilot): spec draft

Owner, 2026-11-20: Farhan mutes other apps' notification sounds by default; a chosen subset still breaks through like phone calls do. Disclaimers are fine; ADB is the recovery path only. Evidence: `research/notification-sound-control.md` (round 1 and 2, API 35 emulator; transcripts in `research/sound-probe/`). Owner decisions today: the Farhan-owned rule + bypass-channel approach is correct; calls mirror the owner's own call settings (the owner will test); the timed-unmute is an experiment, tested alongside; both this pilot and the snooze pilot are built and tested.

Branch: `pilot/sound-control` (new, off the notification pilot base `717faf6`, separate from `pilot/snooze`). Feature flag, default off. Pilot bars (default, owner may change): error-paths 8, durability 8, architecture 7, legibility 7.

## Intent

When on, Farhan holds a Farhan-owned Priority Do Not Disturb rule, so notifications from other apps are silent. A notification Farhan elects to sound is delivered as a Farhan proxy on a Farhan-owned channel that bypasses Do Not Disturb, so it beeps and buzzes while everything else stays silent. Nothing about the owner's own Do Not Disturb is lost: Android keeps and merges the user's state; Farhan only adds and removes its own rule.

## Decisions (defaults taken; the owner may overrule)

| Id | Decision |
|---|---|
| S1 | The mute is an explicit `AutomaticZenRule` owned by Farhan (visible and removable in Android Settings), not the implicit app rule and not the manual zen mode. Its `ZenPolicy` allows calls (see S4), alarms, and (owner option) media; everything else off. Off removes only that rule. |
| S2 | Elected alerts are Farhan notifications on a Farhan-owned channel created with bypass-DND requested, read back, and with an explained recovery action if the user or Android disabled it. They go through the existing proxy path and delivery pipeline (budget, cadence, exceptions), so "elected" means what the existing pipeline already decides to deliver, plus per-app and per-category sound election in settings. The original is cancelled as the proxy path does today. |
| S3 | Per-source sounds (proposal, to verify on device): a Farhan channel per elected source channel, mirroring the source channel's sound and vibration pattern read from the ranking, so an elected message from one app sounds like that app. Fall back to one Farhan channel with the owner's chosen sound when the source channel cannot be read. |
| S4 | Calls: the rule's call policy mirrors the owner's own call settings (who may call, repeat callers), read at enable time and re-read when they change; Farhan's rule never narrows or widens what calls do today. Disclaimer in the settings text that call behaviour with a second active DND rule was tested on one emulator only; the owner tests on their phone. The owner's call screener's notification is CRITICAL in Farhan and untouched. |
| S5 | Persisted state: owned rule id, desired state, generation, last observed effective filter and policy (diagnostic only), timestamps with boot id. Reconcile on listener (re)connect, app start, boot/unlock, a WorkManager fallback, and the filter/policy-changed callbacks, re-reading Android's state rather than trusting callback arguments. If the owner stops or edits Farhan's rule in Settings, latch Paused (never re-enable behind their back); a fresh user action resumes. |
| S6 | A persistent low-importance status notification "Farhan is managing Do Not Disturb" with an Off action and a link to Android's Modes settings, separate from the breakthrough channel. |
| S7 | Disclaimers (shown at enable): the phone can stay muted if Farhan dies with the rule on, until it reconnects or the rule is turned off in Settings; elected alerts carry Farhan's identity and channel sound; the original may leave a second shade entry unless cancelled; a stricter DND mode, a disabled channel or a silent ringer still silences the alert; needs notification access, Do Not Disturb access and permission to post. |
| S8 | The timed-unmute experiment (open window, 0-500 ms to 30 s) is a separate, clearly labelled opt-in under the same flag; it always leaks other apps (measured) and is for the owner's own comparison. Never default. |
| S9 | No ADB in the main path. The recovery path (settings_rescue) may re-grant, nothing else. |
| S10 | New settings are registered in `SettingsCatalog` (rule election per app/category, sound choice) with semantic validation; no rule ids or generations are exported. |

## States and edges

Access not granted (each of three grants, deny and revoke; explain and link to Settings); rule already exists after reinstall (adopt by stored id, else find by name and owner package, never duplicate); the user has a stricter manual mode (the consolidated policy still blocks the alert: say so in the status text); the user turns Farhan's rule off in Settings (Paused); reboot / locked boot; force-stop (needs the user to reopen the app); channel disabled or bypass dropped by the user; a second Farhan rule request while one is in flight; a burst of elected alerts (rate-limit and dedupe by notification key and post time); snooze returns (a snooze return that Farhan elects is delivered through the proxy path; native returns stay silent under the mute; see the snooze spec); time zone and DND schedules owned by the user are not touched.

## Invariants

- Farhan only ever creates, edits and removes the rule it owns (by stored id and owner package). It never calls the global manual zen setters while the explicit-rule API is available.
- With the flag off, no rule exists, no channel is created, and behaviour is byte-for-byte today's.
- Off persists first, then removes the rule; any later timer or worker of an older generation does nothing.
- Calls behave as without Farhan (mirror, verified by the real-call transcripts on the emulator; the owner confirms on their phone).

## Slices (from the research)

1. Grant, own and release one Priority rule (the three grants, explicit rule, effective policy display, Off, status notification). Clean install on API 35 with wireless debugging off.
2. Publish one elected alert on the bypass channel; interleave an independent app and prove the competitor has no beep/buzz while the proxy has both, with no filter transition; per-source channels (S3) behind a sub-flag.
3. Coexist with the owner's changes (reconciler, Paused latch, reboot/force-stop behaviour); call-policy mirroring (S4); timed-unmute experiment (S8).

## Needs before code (build-loop front sequence)

- Mock-up for the settings section, the enable flow with disclaimers and the status notification (orchestrator draws it; owner signs off).
- Spec review by a different model; red tests; the red gate verified by the orchestrator.
- The sound-control research branch `pilot/snooze` commits (research only) are not this pilot's base; this pilot starts from `717faf6` and reads the research files.

## v2 (spec review round 1 and the exchange, 2026-11-20; v2 wins over the draft above)

Review: Opus, 11 musts, verdict CHANGES; after the exchange: OK for a flagged-off, owner-tested pilot of slices 1-2 with the set below. Condensed record: `research/review/sound-spec-review-round1.md`.

### Replaced or struck from the draft
- S4 (mirror the owner's call settings) is REPLACED: the readable policy is the owner's DND-on policy (e.g. starred-only) and mirroring it narrows calls when DND is off (transcripts `calls/api35-calls.txt` rows 7-10). Farhan's rule always allows calls from anyone and repeat callers, which is the identity under strictest-wins: DND off, calls ring as today; the owner's own mode on, their stricter call policy wins. (Owner informed.) Strictest-wins for calls with a second rule is untested: device test required.
- S3 (per-source channels) out. The S5 diagnostic snapshot out. S8 (timed-unmute experiment) moves to slice 3 and stays out of the Held/Off reconciler type.
- The draft sentence "A stricter DND mode of your own still silences them" is false under the default policy (priority channels allowed) and is replaced by the M2 disclosure below.

### The design rule: the reconciler can only release
The reconciler's action type has NO Create or Activate case. Only the enable or resume tap (user-action entry point) creates or activates the rule. Consequences by construction: nothing re-enables behind the owner's back; an imported or restored "On" cannot create a rule; a rule the owner deleted is never recreated; a stop in Settings is shown as "Stopped in Settings, tap to resume" with no Paused latch.

### Must hold for slices 1-2 (flagged-off pilot)
1. Calls: ZenPolicy calls = anyone, repeat callers allowed (fixed values, never read from Android).
2. Full policy: every ZenPolicy field set explicitly (calls anyone; repeat callers on; alarms on; media on by default; system sounds: owner option default on; priority channels on; messages, conversations, reminders, events off; visual effects all shown; device effects null).
3. Orphan cleanup: on app start and on listener connect, regardless of the flag, if no persisted desired-On exists remove every owned rule found by Farhan's fixed `conditionId`. Adopt by stored id, else by conditionId; never by name; never touch a foreign rule.
4. Persist order: `commit()` {desired On, generation} before `addAutomaticZenRule`; crash windows are covered by item 3. Sound-control state uses its own synchronous store, not the `apply()` preferences.
5. Fail-open: release the rule (state Suspended with a reason shown) when the filter switch or app main switch is off, any of the three grants is missing, or the breakthrough channel reads back without bypass or at importance NONE.
6. Channel order: create the breakthrough channel only after policy access is granted, read it back; a bad read-back feeds item 5. Never delete-and-recreate.
7. Off: persist Off first, remove the rule, keep the status notification until removal is confirmed; if removal fails it links to Android's Modes settings.
8. Whole-tree ban (with a positive control) on `setRingerMode`, `setInterruptionFilter`, `setNotificationPolicy`, `requestInterruptionFilter`, `requestListenerHints` outside the future experiment package.
9. The enable key is NOT under the `notification_experiment_` prefix (so it is `Unsupported` in `SettingsCatalog` and never exported); rule id, generation and phase are `Excluded(INTERNAL)`; the sound-control prefs file is excluded from cloud backup and device transfer.
10. `ProxyNotificationPoster.post(item, alert: ProxyAlert)` with `ProxyAlert` = Breakthrough | Normal | Silent decided in the domain; `channelId` threaded through; "elected" is one pure function (`ElectionPolicy`) and a sound attribute on existing deliveries, not an extra delivery decision that overrides the budget; at most one audible alert per batch tick.
11. Elected alerts are never posted for work-profile items.

Architecture: inside `notification_filter`: domain `sound/` (`MutePolicy`, `SoundControlState` Off/Creating/Held/Suspended(reason), `Reconciler`, `ElectionPolicy`); data `sound/` adapters. Ports: `ZenRulePort` (add/update/remove/ownedRules/ruleState/setState/consolidatedPolicy/currentFilter/policyAccess, typed `AccessLost`), `BreakthroughChannelPort`, `GrantsPort`, `SoundStateStore` (synchronous commit), clock/boot id. One `SoundControlController` serialises all rule mutations behind its own Mutex (never nested in `DeliveryGate`).

### Disclosures at enable (instead of code, wait for slice 3)
- "Elected alerts can sound during your own Do Not Disturb and Bedtime modes. To stop that, turn off 'Override Do Not Disturb' for Farhan's alert channel."
- "While muted, only the first message in a conversation sounds until you open or dismiss Farhan's alert." (updates stay silent: M4)
- "If you turn off Farhan's alert override, Farhan turns sound control off; reinstall to reset it."
- "If Farhan stops, is force-stopped or killed by the system, your phone stays muted until you open Farhan or tap Off in the status notification or in Android's Modes settings."
- "Work-profile notifications are silenced too."
- Exception apps and notifications Farhan marks Critical are silent while the rule is held. To keep one audible, allow it in Android's Do Not Disturb app exceptions (Farhan's rule allows priority channels, so any channel the owner sets to bypass keeps working natively). The enable screen lists the owner's exception apps.
- The call screener's CRITICAL notification stays untouched; whether it passes as a call under Farhan's rule needs a test on the owner's phone.
- Calls ring as they do now.

### Red tests (fake ZenRulePort, SoundStateStore; each with why/catches)
Policy fields pinned by name (calls ANY even when the fake readable policy is STARRED); flag off with an owned rule present removes it; a stale stored id is adopted by conditionId with no add; a foreign rule is never touched (positive control: the owned rule is removed); rule missing while desired On adds nothing; each fail-open precondition releases the rule; crash between persist and remove completes on restart; Off persists first; older-generation worker after Off does nothing; `AccessLost` keeps the status and ends in NeedsAccess without a crash loop; the ban test with a positive control; `SettingsCatalog` literal-name classification (enable key `Unsupported`, id/generation/phase `Excluded`); `ElectionPolicy` (CRITICAL and exception items are not elected; same key and post time alerts once; N elected in a tick alerts once; work profile not elected); model-based property test over enable/off/crash/restart/user-stop/revoke sequences (persisted not-On implies no active owned rule; never more than one owned rule; never a foreign mutation; never an activation without a same-generation user action; coverage counter for user-stop and crash-mid-enable).
Emulator (instrumented, API 35): create and read the policy back; competitor silent while the breakthrough proxy alerts (`notification_alert`); a non-starred injected call rings while held with DND off; clear data while held removes the rule on next launch. Robolectric/instrumented: a channel created before access reads back bypass=false and posting returns `Failed("breakthrough_bypass_lost")`.

### Slice 3 (later): edit versus stop adoption, rule-status broadcast, manual invocation decision, M2 per-item option, M4 update re-alert, the dead-man exact alarm, the timed-unmute experiment, per-source sounds.

# Sound control GREEN report

Base RED commit `9c0ff5f`. The sound branch builds and the JVM suites pass. Device results and remaining limits are below.

The spec requires explicit activation and release-only recovery. Android can refuse removal after it revokes DND access. In that case the controller keeps the Modes recovery path. The clear-data test will distinguish an orphan removed by launch from a rule already removed by Android.

## UI inheritance

The settings section will reuse the switch row, card surfaces and typography from the original notification settings and Automation section. The pilot sections and Settings Hub establish grouping and theme surfaces. The signed-off HTML supplies the sound section order, grant steps and disclosure dialog. The status notification uses Android's native notification layout.

## Phases

| Phase | Commit | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Domain | `844cfc0` | Boat Debug JVM suite passed |
| Data | `0bbf344` | Controller, Android rule and channel adapters, durable journal, status and backup exclusions |
| Wiring | `f878525` | App, listener, boot and unlock recovery, generation-aware worker, proxy adapter and settings classification |
| UI | `d07000d`, `ec48ddc` | Sound control settings, election picker, grant/disclosure flow and navigation inset fix |

## Behavior and decisions

- Explicit enable writes On and its generation before adding or activating an owned Priority rule. The written policy allows anyone, repeat callers, alarms, media, system sounds by default, and priority channels. Other sound categories are off and all visual effects are shown. The Android rule has no device effects.
- Recovery matches the exact condition and owner, gives a valid stored ID precedence, removes duplicates and adopts a stale ID without activating it. Off writes first. A denied removal keeps the status and the Android Modes link where Android still allows posting. Restored access lets reconciliation finish a previously blocked release.
- Startup, listener connection, switch changes, permission or channel changes, and the generation-aware WorkManager fallback use the same release path. The controller serializes mutations independently of the delivery gate.
- Android creates the alert channel only with policy access. The poster checks bypass and importance before publishing and asks for reconciliation if the check fails. Election is by selected app or category, with the existing critical and exception behavior and a fail-closed check on the source user in Android's notification key. A tick uses one audible alert only after a successful post.
- The enable flag and rule journal live together in the backup-excluded `sound_control.xml`. Portable configuration contains only app and category elections and the system-sounds option. Import cannot activate a rule.
- The settings screen uses the existing experiment switch row and App Priorities discovery catalog, with a filtered app list. It shows the aggregate Android filter because API 35 does not expose an independent manual-mode value. The pilot uses a single Farhan channel. System-sounds changes take effect the next time the rule is started.

## Boat verification

No RED tests edited. The combined Boat run passed `:app:assembleDebug`, `:notification_filter:notification_filter_data:assembleDebugAndroidTest`, and every JVM test on 2026-11-20.

| Module and variant | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Notification filter domain, Debug JVM | 159 | 0 | 0 |
| Notification filter data, Debug JVM | 44 | 0 | 0 |
| Notification filter presentation, Debug JVM | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Settings portability, JVM | 61 | 0 | 0 |

The debug APK is on Boat at `~/runs/sound-green-codex/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`. The full JVM and APK run passed again after `ec48ddc`. The integration target should take the inset fix as well as the four phase commits.

## Spot mutations

Boat applied each mutation individually and restored the source after its test. The STARRED-call mutation failed the fixed-policy assertion. Removing the one-audible-per-tick guard failed on the two missing Silent alerts. Trusting requested bypass failed the literal `breakthrough_bypass_lost` result assertion. All three failures were Truth assertions.

## API 35 device evidence

| RED instrumented case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Complete policy round trip | Passed. The test read the explicit Priority rule, every ZenPolicy field, its condition ID and null device effects from Android. |
| Pre-grant bypass read-back | Passed. Android retained HIGH importance and stripped bypass. Breakthrough posting returned `Failed("breakthrough_bypass_lost")`. |
| Unfamiliar first call | Passed. A fresh GSM number rang with an unmuted Telecom ringtone before hold. A different fresh number rang while Farhan held Priority. |
| Independent competitor and proxy | The original test fails at the positive control before enabling. Its component token is quoted when passed to UiAutomation's direct command launcher. A host broadcast to the same component did emit a beep and buzz. A supplemental run without the quotes recorded a beep and buzz for competitor ID `13442484` before hold and for proxy `verified-13442485` while held. Competitor ID `13442485` was present in the system dump and emitted no alert event. The final check for a still-active proxy failed because it had already disappeared from the app's active list. The effective filter was Priority before and after the supplemental post. Continuous transition monitoring from the original case remains unverified. [Android 15 UiAutomation command launcher](https://github.com/aosp-mirror/platform_frameworks_base/blob/android-15.0.0_r1/core/java/android/app/UiAutomationConnection.java#L550-L554) |
| Clear data and relaunch | The original case names the existing alpha installation. The existing alpha v8 data was preserved, so the original test was not run. On the disposable `.soundpilot` build, the held rule survived `pm clear`. Launch removed that rule from the live Android configuration and returned DND to Off. |

A first invocation after installing the library test APK may crash in the existing Hilt delivery receiver as Android delivers a queued broadcast to the library's plain Application. Retrying the same case after that delivery allowed the policy tests to execute. The RED files were unchanged.

The shared alpha install uses Room schema v8. The sound branch is based on schema v7. The attempted same-ID launch reported a missing 8→7 migration. Reinstalling the Boat snooze build restored the v8 app and it launched again. Device checks restored DND off, Silent ringer, navigation mode 0 and the original listener grant. Temporary instrumentation, probe and screenshot apps were removed. The original light system theme was restored.

Reboot, locked boot, physical calls on the owner's phone, work-profile behavior on a real device, and OEM-specific rule behavior remain unverified.

## UI fidelity

Six [screenshot pairs](../captures/sound-control/pairs/) compare the signed-off HTML on the left with the fixed build on the right. Each panel uses a 1080 × 1920 viewport. Boat Chromium rendered the HTML with its original light and dark styles and each panel expanded to the device viewport. The build used Farhan's inherited colors and typography and Android's native system bars.

| Screen | Visible differences |
| --- | --- |
| Settings | The app toolbar is taller and the system navigation bar uses device space. Farhan's light palette is white and lavender with amber actions. Its dark palette uses black and gray with amber actions. Both themes use larger, filled Material cards, more vertical spacing, and a native switch. The default switch is off and the live election counts are zero. The election button replaces the draft Breakthrough heading. Sound uses one Farhan channel, a channel Settings link and a system-sounds switch in place of the draft per-app sound mirroring. The call row displays the v2 policy. The aggregate filter and Android Modes action sit below the first viewport. The timed-unmute section is deferred to slice 3. |
| Enable flow | Three filled cards use text labels in place of numbered circles. The captured test app has all three grants, so the cards show Allowed and the grant buttons are hidden. The intro is shorter. The v2 disclosures use separate paragraphs inside the card and continue below the first viewport. The confirmation scrolls into view. The first capture exposed three-button navigation overlapping the confirmation. `ec48ddc` reserves that inset, and the confirmation tapped successfully in light and dark. |
| Status | Android supplies the clock, status icons, quick-settings tiles, Silent section, app icon, expansion control, Manage button and separate light/dark surfaces. The real notification uses the Farhan-alpha label and the requested title, with release instructions in the body and Off and Android Modes actions. # Sound control pilot: code and UI fidelity review, round 1

Reviewer: Opus (review sub-agent). Scope: `git diff 717faf6..556cc02` on `pilot/sound-control`, read in full for the domain `sound/` package, the data `sound/` adapters, the controller, the runtime, the receiver and worker, the proxy poster, the coordinator change, the `NotificationService` wiring, the DI module, the backup rules, the `SettingsCatalog` and validator, and `SoundControlSettingsScreen`. I read the tests named below. I did not run Gradle. Bar: pilot (only stranding, lost notifications, consent bypass, data loss or crash).

## Findings

**F1 [blocker]** `notification_filter_domain/.../delivery/NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:275-276` together with `notification_filter_data/.../service/NotificationService.kt:327` and `notification_filter_data/.../sound/SoundProxyNotificationPoster.kt:23-28`.
When a Breakthrough post fails (`breakthrough_bypass_lost`), the coordinator returns `PostFailed`. `NotificationService` then cancels the source notification anyway, because line 327 cancels on every outcome except `Cleared`. A batch-cadence item is retried on the next tick, and by then the reconcile request has released the rule, so it posts as Normal. An item on an `IMMEDIATELY` cadence is never retried, because `shouldDeliverOnBatchTick` excludes `IMMEDIATELY` and `onArrival` is the only path that delivers it.
Failure scenario: the owner sets HIGH to Immediately and elects Messenger. Following the enable disclosure, they turn off "Override Do Not Disturb" on Farhan's alert channel. Nothing reconciles right away, because no broadcast fires for a bypass toggle. `ACTION_NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL_BLOCK_STATE_CHANGED` covers blocking only, and `onNotificationChannelModified` is not delivered for Farhan's own channels to a non-companion listener. The next Messenger message is elected. The poster reads `usable == false` and returns Failed. The original is cancelled and no proxy is posted. The message is gone from the shade and stays only in Farhan's in-app list. The owner was told it would sound. Default settings never hit this, because only CRITICAL is Immediately and CRITICAL is never elected. Any owner who sets a non-critical priority to Immediately can hit it.
Smallest fix: in `deliver()`, if `alert == Breakthrough` and the post fails, call `postSafely(item, alert = ProxyAlert.Normal)` once and use that result. The poster keeps its literal `Failed("breakthrough_bypass_lost")` contract and its red test, and still calls `bypassLost()`, so the rule is still released. Add one coordinator test: an elected Immediately item with a poster that fails Breakthrough ends `Delivered` with a Normal post.

**F2 [should]** `notification_filter_data/.../sound/SoundControlController.kt:95-98`.
`off()` refuses to remove the rule when the Off journal commit fails. It returns a recovery status and the phone stays muted after the owner tapped Off. Under the release-only design, removing without a durable Off is safe. On restart, `desiredOn = true` with no rule plans `STOPPED_IN_SETTINGS`, and nothing is recreated. Holding the mute protects nothing. The scenario is rare: `SharedPreferences.commit()` returns false, for example on a full disk. It is still a path where an explicit Off leaves the phone muted. The recovery text and the Modes link make it recoverable, so this is not a blocker.
Smallest fix: on a failed commit, still run the release. Remove every owned rule by conditionId, then return `Suspended(STORAGE_FAILED)` with the recovery status only if a rule remains.

**F3 [should; owner decision, no change recommended for the pilot]** K2 "listener dead".
`onListenerDisconnected` (`NotificationService.kt`) requests a reconcile, but the reconciler only checks the listener *grant* (`AndroidSoundGrants.kt:19`), not whether the listener is bound. If Android unbinds the listener while the process lives and the grant stays, the rule stays held. No proxies are posted, so elected alerts do not sound. The other apps' originals stay in the shade, silent, because the policy shows every visual effect. So nothing is lost, and the status notification's Off action still works through `SoundControlReceiver`. Releasing on disconnect would need a resume tap after every transient rebind under the release-only rule, which is worse for the owner. Spec v2 item 5 lists grants, not binding, and the enable disclosure covers "If Farhan stops". I would keep it and name it in the device test list.

No other findings at the pilot bar.

## Invariants checked

- **K1, release only.** The `ReconcileAction` type has only `Adopt` and `Release` (`Reconciler.kt:3-6`). `rules.add`, `rules.update` and `setState(active = true)` are called only inside `SoundControlController.enable()`. `enable()` has exactly two callers: the button `I understand, turn it on`, which needs all three grants (`SoundControlSettingsScreen.kt:225-228`), and the instrumented fixture. The switch row only navigates to the enable page. The worker, boot, unlock, listener and app-start paths all call `reconcile()`. `accessLost()` also commits `desiredOn = false`, so a re-grant cannot resume the mute without a tap. Holds.
- **K2, fail open.** The release happens when the filter is off, the main switch is off, any of the three grants is missing, or the channel is missing, has bypass off or has importance NONE (`Reconciler.kt:20-24, 44-51`). `SoundFailOpenTest` covers all eight cases. Real policy-access revoke: `withPolicyAccess` throws `AccessLost` before the fake's remove is reached. On a real device, Android Settings deletes the app's rules when it revokes zen access, and the recovery status with the Modes link covers the rest. POST revoke kills the process, and the system rebinds the listener, which reconciles. Holds, except for the trade-off in F3.
- **K3, orphans.** `onAppStart` (Application `start()` → `requestReconcile`) and `onListenerConnected` release every rule matching owner package and `condition://<pkg>/sound-control` when the flag is off or `desiredOn` is false (`Reconciler.kt:17-20`). `owns()` matches by package and condition, never by name (`AndroidZenRulePort.kt:97-99`). The controller test proves both entries leave foreign and unrelated rules alone. The device clear-data check passed on the disposable build. Holds.
- **K4, enable key.** `notification_sound_control_enabled` and the journal live in `sound_control.xml`, which is excluded from full backup, cloud backup and device transfer. The key is `Unsupported` in `SettingsCatalog` and the journal keys are `Excluded(INTERNAL)`. Only the elections and system sounds are portable. Even a restored `phase=on` cannot create or activate a rule, because of K1. Holds.
- **K5, policy.** `MutePolicy.forPilot` plus `toAndroidPolicy` set every field: calls anyone, repeat callers, alarms, media, system sounds (owner option), priority channels, messages, conversations, reminders and events off, and all visual effects shown. The device round trip passed. Holds.
- **K6, channel order.** `AndroidBreakthroughChannel.create()` returns early without policy access. It is called only from `enable()` after `suspensionBeforeChannel()` is null. `NotificationService` creates only the standard proxy channel. Holds.
- **K7, updates.** An already-delivered item takes `refresh` → `ProxyAlert.Silent` on the standard channel. Breakthrough posts carry `setOnlyAlertOnce(true)`, and the coordinator dedupes by `(key, postTime)` and allows one audible alert per tick. Holds.
- **K8, the owner's DND.** No call to `setInterruptionFilter`, `setNotificationPolicy`, `setRingerMode`, `requestInterruptionFilter` or `requestListenerHints` anywhere outside tests (grep). `consolidatedPolicy()` is never called by the controller, and a test pins that. The effective filter is shown only in the settings screen. Farhan does not record the owner's prior state, and spec v2 does not need it, because Android merges rules and Farhan only removes its own. Holds.
- **Double posts and unshown notifications.** The Breakthrough and Normal channels share the proxy slot, so the proxy is replaced, not duplicated. A post on `CommitPending` is not re-posted. Non-elected items while held post Silent and stay visible. The only path where a notification is never shown is F1.
- **Crash.** `operation()` maps `AccessLost` and `IllegalArgumentException`. The status `notify` catches `SecurityException`. `electionFor` short-circuits below API 35 before `isManagedProfile`. I found no reachable crash.

## UI fidelity

I viewed all six pairs. Ranked by how much the owner would notice:

1. **Enable screen, disclosure length.** The v2 copy is six paragraphs in a filled card, against the mock's four bullets, so the confirm button sits two viewports down. After `ec48ddc` it scrolls into view above the navigation bar and the green report confirms the tap in both themes. It is not hidden. The stuck-mute sentence is present and accurate: "If Farhan stops, your phone can stay muted. Tap Off in the status notification, open Farhan and turn it off, or stop Farhan's rule in Android Modes." Matches the mock's intent. The mock's "A stricter DND mode … still silences them" and "Calls follow your own call settings" lines were correctly replaced by the v2 wording. These are not contradictions.
2. **Settings, switch state.** In the capture the main switch is off, against On in the mock, because the capture was taken before enabling. The live counts are 0. This is not a defect.
3. **Settings, section structure.** The mock has blue section headers (Breakthrough, Calls, Status, Experiments) above white outlined cards. The build uses a title inside each filled card, and the Status card falls below the first viewport. The election entry is an amber text button rather than a row title. All controls are reachable and labelled. The Experiments section is deferred to slice 3, which is correct per v2.
4. **Enable screen, grant steps.** The mock shows numbered and checked circles. The build shows cards reading "Allowed", with the buttons hidden once granted. Usable.
5. **Status notification.** The build uses the native layout with the title "Farhan is managing Do Not Disturb", the body "Tap Off to release Farhan's mode." and the actions OFF and ANDROID MODES. It sits in Silent (low importance). It matches the mock except for the body text, where the mock reads "Priority only. Other apps are silent." This is not a contradiction.
6. **Theme.** The build follows Farhan's palette (lavender or gray with amber), while the mock is blue. Dark mode is consistent.

Component reuse: this base has no settings-hub section or row components (grep finds no `SettingsSection` or `SettingsRow`). The screen reuses the existing `ExperimentRow` from `AutomationSettingsSection` (made `internal`), Material3 `Card`, `TopAppBar` and theme typography and colors, and adds no custom colors or theme overrides. That is the right inheritance for this base. When it merges into the integration branch that has the settings hub, port `SoundCard` and the in-card titles to the hub's section and row components. That is integration work, not a pilot blocker.

Nothing makes a control unusable, hides the enable confirmation, or contradicts the copy.

# Sound control code review r1: exchange

Answers to the orchestrator's three challenges. Read-only; evidence is from `556cc02`.

## (1) F1 fix shape

**No partial success, no double post.** The Breakthrough failure is decided before any publish. `SoundProxyNotificationPoster.kt:24-28` reads the channel and, if it is not `usable`, calls `bypassLost()` and returns `PostResult.Failed("breakthrough_bypass_lost")` without calling `publish`. The poster test pins `calls == ["read"]` and `posts.isEmpty()` (`SoundProxyNotificationPosterTest.kt:55-57`). In the real publish (`NotificationService.postProxyNotification`, `NotificationService.kt:127-165`), `manager.notify(...)` is the last statement before `PostResult.Posted`, and every `Failed` reason is returned before `notify`. An exception becomes `Failed("notification_post_failed")` in `postSafely` (`NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:297-306`), so a thrown exception cannot follow a completed notify inside `publish`. A double post could not duplicate anyway: every proxy is posted as tag `PROXY_TAG + item.id` with id `1`, so a second post replaces the first.

**Where the failure is visible.** As `PostResult.Failed(reason)` returned from `poster.post(item, alert)` into `postSafely`, then mapped to `DeliveryOutcome.PostFailed` at `NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:275-276`.

**Run the fallback only for `breakthrough_bypass_lost`.** The other reasons fail the standard channel just the same: `notification_permission_denied`, `notifications_disabled`, `proxy_capacity_reached` and `notification_post_failed`. `notification_channel_disabled` cannot come from the breakthrough channel, because `usable` already requires importance above 0; only a read-to-notify race could produce it. A fallback for those reasons would only repeat the failure.

**Smallest change, independent of either `deliver` signature.** Put it in `postSafely`, which neither branch changes:

```kotlin
val first = if (refresh) poster.refresh(item) else poster.post(item, alert)
if (alert == ProxyAlert.Breakthrough && first == PostResult.Failed(BYPASS_LOST)) poster.post(item, ProxyAlert.Normal) else first
```

Share the literal as a domain constant used by the poster. This leaves the poster's red test and the instrumented `Failed("breakthrough_bypass_lost")` assertion valid.

One side effect: `deliver()` then sees `Posted` with `alert == Breakthrough`. It records the identity in `alerted` and sets `sound.alerted`, which silences one more elected alert in that tick. That is harmless, but if you want it exact, have `postSafely` return the effective alert too. I would not, for the pilot.

The fallback should be Normal, not Silent. While the rule is still held, the standard channel is muted by Farhan's rule, so the message is visible and silent. After the reconcile releases the rule, Normal sounds the way the owner's existing settings would.

An alternative inside the poster, falling back to `publish(item, standardChannelId, false)`, breaks two RED assertions: the unit test and `SoundControlPolicyInstrumentedTest.kt:76`. So `postSafely` is the smaller change.

## (2) F1 reach

**CRITICAL and exception items are unaffected.** At `NotificationService.kt:321`, `passThrough` is true for system-exempt items, exception apps and every CRITICAL item. `onArrival` returns `Delivered` before any post when `passThrough` is set (`NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:183`). Line 327 does not cancel pass-through items. `ElectionPolicy.alert` excludes CRITICAL and exceptions anyway. So an elected alert lost from the shade needs a non-critical priority set to Immediately. My earlier claim that default settings never hit this stands.

**Batch-tick items are bounded to one tick, not retried forever.** On the failed tick, `bypassLost` is `soundControl::requestReconcile` (`NotificationFilterDataModule.kt`). That reconcile sees `channel.usable == false`, plans `Suspended(CHANNEL_UNUSABLE)` and releases (`Reconciler.kt:22-24`). Even if the release fails (`REMOVAL_FAILED`) or access is lost, the state is `Suspended`, never `Held`. `SoundControlRuntime.electionFor` returns `null` unless the state is `Held` (`SoundControlRuntime.kt:161`). So on the next tick the alert is `ProxyAlert.Normal` and it posts. Nothing returns the state to `Held` without an enable tap (K1). The failure therefore cannot repeat.

**The queue is held for one cadence period.** Each tick takes one head per (package, priority) (`NotificationFilterDataModule.kt` `pending`, `NotificationDao.pendingHead`), and `nextHead` is pulled only after `Delivered` (`NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:245-247`). A `PostFailed` head therefore holds that app and priority until the next tick: an hour for HIGH, a day for LOW, with the defaults. That is a delay, not a permanent block. With the F1 fallback in `postSafely`, the failing tick itself delivers and nothing is held.

There is a pre-existing, unrelated risk: a head that fails for a reason that never clears, such as `proxy_capacity_reached`, holds its group. That is outside this pilot.

## (3) F2: removing the rule when saving Off fails

**Nothing recreates it (K1).** Only `enable()` calls `rules.add` or `setState(true)` (grep: `SoundControlRuntime.kt:119` and the instrumented fixture). After the removal, the journal still says `desiredOn = true, ruleId = X`. On the next reconcile, `plan` finds no owned rule, so `preferredRule` is null and the state is `Suspended(STOPPED_IN_SETTINGS)` with no actions (`Reconciler.kt:26-34`). The worker stays scheduled, because `scheduleFallback` sees `desiredOn`, and every run takes the same release-only path.

**The status and settings show the true state, not On.**
- Status notification: the reconcile result is not `Held`, so the `else` branch calls `clearStatus()` (`SoundControlController.kt:139-147`). The ruleId-clearing commit runs only when there is a `Release` action or `!desiredOn`, so it is skipped, and no failed commit is hit there. In `off()` itself, the fix should call `clearStatus()` once the rule is confirmed gone, and keep the recovery status only if a rule remains.
- Settings switch: checked only for `Held` or `Creating` (`SoundControlSettingsScreen.kt:140`), so it shows off.
- Wording: in the same session the status line reads `STORAGE_FAILED`: "Could not save the change. Check Android Modes before trying again." That is accurate. After a restart it reads "Stopped in Settings. Turn on sound control to resume." The mute state is right but the cause is wrong. That is cosmetic and fine for the pilot.
- Elections stop, because `electionFor` needs `Held`.
- `setPilotFlag(false)` is skipped. That is harmless, because the flag alone cannot activate anything.

## Anything else that should block the pilot

No.
